chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'God did not send a prophet at any time except that, in God's knowledge, when He perfected his religion, the prohibition of wine was included in it. Thus, wine remained forbidden, and they were only transferred from one stage to another. And if that prohibition had been imposed upon them all at once, they would have been cut off from the religion.'

He said, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'No one is more gentle than God, exalted and mighty. Among His gentleness is that He transferred them from one stage to another. And if He had imposed it upon them all at once, they would have perished.'
ai.seo_question: Why was the prohibition of wine not revealed all at once in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates the divine wisdom behind the gradual prohibition of wine, noting that while the ruling was eternally known to God, it was revealed in stages to accommodate human capacity. This pedagogical approach of 'rifq' (gentleness) ensured that the community could internalize the prohibition without being overwhelmed, thereby preserving the continuity of the religion rather than causing its abandonment.
